content.title: About
content.content: Relish is marinated corn prepared in a traditional recipe with vinegar, spices, and a touch of sugar. The kernels stay crisp while acquiring a mildly sweet‑sour flavor characteristic of relish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Relish is a popular bar and restaurant snack, especially in the United States.
Traditional recipes use gelatin to keep the kernels firm in the jar.
Sweet, large‑kernel corn varieties are chosen for the best taste.
Some regions add smoked paprika for a subtle smoky aroma.
Properly canned relish can be stored for up to a year.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Corn provides fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies thiamine, niacin, and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin in corn help protect the eyes from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many snack foods, marinated corn is low in fat.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Carbohydrates in corn quickly provide the body with energy.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The brine can be high in sodium, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience an allergic reaction to corn.

items.title: Added sugar
items.content: Some recipes include sugar, increasing the product’s calorie count.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Commercially produced relish may contain preservatives that not everyone tolerates.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Relish can be enjoyed straight from the jar, added to salads, tacos, burritos, or used as a side for meat dishes. Drain excess brine before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep an opened jar of relish refrigerated and sealed with its lid. When stored properly, it remains flavorful for 2‑3 weeks. Discard if the smell or taste changes.
